item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
Mostly negative, with a few real but limited inclusion-oriented actions. Tshisekedi’s 2024 record shows targeted support for girls, disabled students, poor provinces, and vulnerable families, but the dominant pattern is that conflict, repression, and underfunding left marginalized groups exposed rather than clearly prioritized.

**Accepted Claims**
- **Democratic Republic of Congo: Expanding and Equipping Primary School Classrooms for Better Learning Outcomes** | World Bank | 2024-02-28 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/02/28/democratic-republic-of-congo-afe-expanding-and-equipping-primary-school-classrooms-for-better-learning-outcomes | The project explicitly aimed at equitable access for girls and students with disabilities, plus better classrooms, learning materials, teacher quality, decentralized planning, and school water/sanitation. Strong positive evidence for prioritizing children, girls, disabled people, and poorer provinces, though still project-level rather than proof of nationwide delivery. | IDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `6B.1`

- **Strengthening Public Social Spending in DRC** | IMF | 2024 | https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/227/article-A002-en.xml | The IMF said social spending increased and education and health were prioritized, with free primary education expanding access. This is real positive evidence for vulnerable groups, especially children, but it also notes social protection remained very weak. | IDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `6B.1`

- **UNICEF cash transfers help build community resilience** | UNICEF DRC | 2024-06-18 | https://www.unicef.org/drcongo/en/stories/unicef-cash-transfers-help-build-community-resilience | UNICEF described cash transfers helping families eat better, keep children in school, and access health care, with explicit goals of reducing food insecurity, malnutrition, displacement, and barriers to services. This is positive evidence for poor households and children, but it is limited in scale and not the same as state-wide prioritization. | IDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `6B.1`

- **In the water sector, taking stock of challenges leads to new solutions** | World Bank | 2024-06-10 | https://connect4impact.worldbank.org/topic/democratic-republic-congo-water-sector-taking-stock-challenges-leads-new-solutions | The World Bank said DRC still had very low water and sanitation access, but the government-backed PASEA program was launched to expand basic drinking water and sanitation in selected provinces. This is positive for poor regions and service access, but it is still early-stage and geographically limited. | IDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`

- **DRC: President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis** | Amnesty International | 2024-06-24 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/ | Amnesty said public resources were being squandered, essential services were underfunded, and this was harming rights to food, healthcare, water, sanitation, education, and housing. That is strong negative evidence that vulnerable groups were not being treated as the priority of rule. | IDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `6B.1`

- **Democratic Republic of Congo battle worsens as hunger deepens** | United Nations | 2024-03-27 | https://press.un.org/en/2024/sc15646.doc.htm | The UN said eastern Congo’s crisis had worsened, with massive displacement and acute hunger, and that one Congolese person in four faced hunger and malnutrition. This is strong negative evidence for poor regions, displaced people, and food-security priorities. | IDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`

- **DRC President Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations** | Amnesty International | 2024-09-30 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/ | Amnesty said shelter, food, healthcare, and education needs remained chronically underfunded and that the state of siege militarized everyday life. This points to welfare being subordinated to coercive control rather than vulnerable-group protection. | IDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `6B.1`

- **Democratic Republic of Congo country chapter** | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/democratic-republic-congo | HRW said corruption and repression reduced the government’s capacity to deliver quality education, health care, and social security, while abuses continued against civilians and critics. This is negative evidence against sustained prioritization of marginalized communities. | IDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `6B.1`

- **More than 260 women sexually assaulted during Congo prison break, UN report shows** | Reuters | 2024-09-12 | https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/More-than-260-women-sexually-assaulted-during-Congo-prison-break-UN-reports-shows-47860482/ | Reuters reported prison guards used live fire during the Makala escape attempt, killing at least 129 people, and that more than 260 female inmates were sexually assaulted. This is severe negative evidence for the protection of women and other vulnerable people in state custody. | IDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `6B.1`

- **Airstrike kills nine in displacement camp near Goma** | Reuters | 2024-05-03 | https://www.yahoo.com/news/airstrike-kills-nine-displacement-camp-110342393.html | Reuters reported nine civilians, including seven children, were killed in a strike on a displacement camp near Goma. Even with responsibility unclear, this is negative evidence that displaced children and other vulnerable civilians were not reliably protected. | IDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `6B.1`

**Search Gap**
- I found no strong 2024 evidence of a sustained national program that clearly prioritized elderly people, ethnic minorities, or disabled people across budgets and delivery systems.
- The positive evidence is mostly project-based, humanitarian, or pilot-scale, not proof of durable nationwide prioritization.
- I did not find a clean government outcome series for service coverage by group, so the strongest conclusion rests on a mix of targeted positives and broad negative humanitarian/rights reporting.
